mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased business costs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the past month, the combined effect signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the past month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 200,000 does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 1% over the past month, the combined effect signals a shift from production to consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and INDPRO decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of RSAFS increase > 1% and INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points over the past month signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.25pp does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).
